questions: Can Redwood meet p95 <120ms for 64-token responses at 150 concurrency?
How does streaming affect token/sec and p95 calculations?

transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45-ish minutes, wanna cover latency/throughput and then talk Hosted vs Dedicated options. Lina, do you wanna kick off with your high-level goals?
[00:00:12] Lina (CTO, AnthemPay): yeah uh thanks Jordan. We run a real-time fraud model in inference path for authorization flows. p95 is super important — ideally under 120 millis for short prompts, worst case we can tolerate up to 200ms but that's not great. We're currently hitting around 300-400ms p95 on our self-hosted endpoints.
[00:00:35] Raj (Lead ML): to add, typical sequence lengths are small, around 32-64 tokens, but we also have some longer contexts for investigation workflows. Concurrency is the pain point, we expect 150-200 concurrent queries at peak, streaming is also used for partial outputs in our UI.
[00:00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): okay good context. Quick note on streaming — it can increase perceived latency for first token but reduces time-to-first-byte overall; for p95 we usually measure until first useful token or full response depending on app. For short completions we can optimize kernels and batching to keep p95 low.
[00:01:05] Maya (SRE): when you say batching, are we talking about server-side aggregation that delays requests? Our product needs <120ms end-to-end, user-facing, so we can't accept batching-induced head-of-line delays.
[00:01:20] Ethan (Redwood SE): right, Redwood does continuous batching with latency SLOs — you can set SLO-specific policies that trade throughput vs latency. For strict p95 targets we size Dedicated capacity to keep queueing minimal. In Hosted we also have low-latency tiers and routing.
[00:01:36] Lina: can you give a concrete example — like what token/sec and latency you'd expect on Dedicated versus Hosted for our profile?
[00:01:44] Priya: sure. For a 64-token completion on an optimized quantized model, on a dedicated A100-ish pool we typically hit ~800-1200 tokens/sec per GPU for generation workloads depending on batch and kernel selection; p95 numbers for single-turn short sequences can be ~60-120ms at moderate concurrency when autoscaled correctly. On hosted lower-latency tiers we provide similar numbers but with multi-tenant tradeoffs — for predictable p95 at 150 concurrency we recommend Dedicated.
[00:02:10] Raj: 800-1200 tokens/sec per GPU — ok that helps. How do you measure p95? Is it from request received to last token? first token? We need consistency with our instrumentation.
[00:02:21] Jordan: good callout. We provide both time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token p50/p95 metrics in the console. For UI streaming you may care about time-to-first-token p95 more. We'll share the benchmark template so you can map to your telemetry.
[00:02:34] Owen (PM): what about concurrency scaling — will Dedicated autoscale quick enough when you jump from 20 to 200 requests per second? We have spikey traffic after card declines.
[00:02:44] Priya: Dedicated supports fast autoscale and burst capacity; policies can be conservative to keep p95 stable. There's also warm-pool options and pre-warmed instances for predictable spikes. For the most aggressive SLAs we recommend reserved capacity with headroom.
[00:02:56] Maya: security wise we need SOC2, audit logs, and KMS integration — if we go Private we want customer-managed keys and VPC peering.
[00:03:06] Ethan: Private (VPC) supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and direct network peering; audit logs and SAML SSO are available. Hosted has SOC2 and encrypted-at-rest but Keys are BYOK only on private. We'll include the security pack.
[00:03:18] Raj: back to benchmarking — can we run a token/sec bench against both Hosted and Dedicated with our workload? We want the same prompt set, streaming on for part of it.
[00:03:28] Jordan: absolutely — standard approach is to run a controlled bench with your prompt samples and concurrency profile; we'll run a Redwood-hosted run and a Dedicated run in our lab to compare p95 and tokens/sec. We'll share the template and you can upload traces.
[00:03:40] Lina: fine, but what's realistic for p95 with streaming enabled? We noticed time-to-first-token was okay but time-to-last-token jumped.
[00:03:48] Priya: streaming changes the math — time-to-first-token is mostly model startup and KV lookups; time-to-last-token scales with tokens produced. For short completions, time-to-last-token is still small; if you stream with many small chunks it adds overhead. We recommend measuring both.
[00:04:02] Raj: do you support prefix/KV caching? We have repeated contexts for known customers which should be cached.
[00:04:09] Ethan: yes, we have KV/prefix caching to reduce per-token compute; it dramatically improves tokens/sec for repeated contexts and reduces p95. But caching semantics vary by deployment: Hosted caching is global/multi-tenant optimized, Dedicated/Private supports customer-local caches with stronger guarantees.
[00:04:23] Maya: any notes on quantization? We're looking to reduce cost while keeping latency tight.
[00:04:28] Priya: Quantization helps; our Optimize toolkit recommends quant profiles based on workload. Some quant formats slightly increase token/sec but may add a few ms; often net gain in throughput. We'll include model-specific recommendations in the benchmark report.
[00:04:41] Lina: ok let's talk p95 target concretely — if we aim for p95 <=120ms for 64 tokens at 150 concurrency, what would be the recommended configuration?
[00:04:51] Priya: likely a Dedicated pool with 4-6 GPUs (depending on model size and kernel perf) with autoscale headroom, prefer low-latency kernel selection, and enable prefix caching where possible. We'll propose a sizing sketch after we see your traffic profile.
[00:05:06] Raj: can you estimate cost delta between Hosted low-latency tier vs Dedicated reserved? Even ballpark is useful.
[00:05:12] Jordan: Hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be cheaper early, but Dedicated provides better unit economics at sustained high concurrency due to reserved capacity. We'll include pricing bands in the follow-up.
[00:05:21] Owen: what about graceful degradation — if Dedicated runs out of capacity do you fall back to smaller model or Hosted endpoints?
[00:05:27] Ethan: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or to Hosted endpoints depending on policy. Canary rollouts and automatic fallback keep your app online. We can show config examples.
[00:05:38] Maya: in the benchmarking run, can we test fallback scenarios and cold-starts too? We wanna see p95 under degradation.
[00:05:44] Priya: absolutely, we can simulate spikes and capacity exhaustion to show p95 impacts and fallback behavior.
[00:05:51] Raj: small nit — sometimes Fireflies transcription messes up product names, I might refer to KV cache as K V cache in notes, sorry if that shows up.
[00:05:58] (laughs) Jordan: noted. We'll also put all these notes in the CRM.
[00:06:02] Lina: cool. Any blockers on our side? We'll need to share traces and decide if we can open a temporary Dedicated eval.
[00:06:09] Jordan: no blockers — next steps: we'll send benchmark template and security pack; Raj to share traces; Priya to schedule Dedicated sizing with Maya.
[00:06:17] Owen: timeline: if we get the traces this week, can we run benches next week?
[00:06:21] Priya: yes, bench runs typically take 2-3 days to set up and execute per deployment profile; we'll aim for next-week runs.
[00:06:27] Lina: perfect. Thanks everyone.
[00:06:30] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and pricing, chat soon.
[00:06:34] [call ends]
